# Data displays - Practice Test - Year 9

Attempt all questions and show your working. Suggested time: 30 to 35 minutes.

## Section A: Consolidating (Questions 1-4)

**Question 1**

For each set of data, state whether it is categorical or numerical. If it is numerical, also state whether it is discrete or continuous.

(a) The number of siblings each student in a class has

(b) The favourite colour of each student in a class

(c) The time taken by each runner to finish a $5 \text{ km}$ fun run

(d) The T-shirt size (S, M, L or XL) ordered by each member of a netball club

**Question 2**

Name the most suitable type of display for each set of data.

(a) The maximum temperature in a town each day for a month

(b) The favourite fruit of $30$ students, chosen from apple, banana, mango and orange

(c) The heights, in centimetres, of $50$ students

(d) The number of hours $20$ students studied for a test and the score each student got on the test

**Question 3**

The stem-and-leaf plot shows the ages of $15$ people in a fitness class. Key: $3 \mid 4$ means $34$ years.

| Stem | Leaf |
|---|---|
| 1 | 8 9 |
| 2 | 2 5 5 7 |
| 3 | 0 1 4 8 |
| 4 | 2 5 6 |
| 5 | 1 3 |

Find:

(a) the youngest and the oldest age

(b) the range

(c) the median age

(d) the mode

**Question 4**

A column graph shows how many Year 9 students chose each elective subject. The heights of the columns are: Art $24$, Drama $18$, Music $12$ and Woodwork $26$.

(a) How many students are shown on the graph altogether?

(b) What percentage of these students chose Music?

(c) How many more students chose Woodwork than Drama?

## Section B: Standard (Questions 5-16)

**Question 5**

The heights of $40$ students were measured and grouped into this frequency table, which was then used to draw a histogram. The height is $h$ cm.

| Height (cm) | $150 \le h < 155$ | $155 \le h < 160$ | $160 \le h < 165$ | $165 \le h < 170$ | $170 \le h < 175$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 3 | 7 | 12 | 10 | 8 |

(a) Which class is the modal class?

(b) What percentage of the students are at least $165 \text{ cm}$ tall?

(c) Which class contains the median height? Explain how you know.

(d) Explain why a histogram, rather than a column graph with gaps between the columns, is used for this data.

**Question 6**

A dot plot shows the number of goals a soccer team scored in each of its $20$ matches. The number of dots above each value is shown in the table.

| Goals scored | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of dots | 3 | 6 | 5 | 4 | 1 | 1 |

Find:

(a) the mode

(b) the median

(c) the mean

(d) the range

**Question 7**

The back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot shows the test scores (out of $100$) of two classes, each with $11$ students. Class A's leaves are on the left and are read from the stem outwards. Key: $2 \mid 5 \mid 6$ means $52$ for Class A and $56$ for Class B.

| Class A | Stem | Class B |
|---|---|---|
| | 4 | 5 |
| 8 2 | 5 | 6 |
| 7 4 1 | 6 | 3 8 |
| 8 5 3 0 | 7 | 4 7 9 |
| 4 | 8 | 2 5 8 |
| 1 | 9 | 6 |

(a) Find the median score for each class.

(b) Find the range of scores for each class.

(c) Which class did better overall? Give a reason.

(d) Which class had more consistent scores? Give a reason.

**Question 8**

A café recorded the number of customers it had each day for $60$ days. The box plot of the data has:

minimum $40$, lower quartile $55$, median $68$, upper quartile $80$, maximum $110$.

(a) Find the range.

(b) Find the interquartile range.

(c) On about what percentage of the days did the café have more than $80$ customers?

(d) On about how many of the $60$ days did the café have between $55$ and $68$ customers?

**Question 9**

The number of minutes $11$ students spent on homework one night was:

$24, \ 15, \ 31, \ 18, \ 12, \ 26, \ 22, \ 40, \ 17, \ 29, \ 21$

(a) Find the five-number summary. (Do not include the median in either half when finding the quartiles.)

(b) Find the interquartile range.

(c) A box plot is drawn from this data. Which whisker is longer, the left (lower) whisker or the right (upper) whisker? Show how you know.

**Question 10**

In a survey, $72$ people were asked to name their favourite season.

| Season | Summer | Autumn | Winter | Spring |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of people | 30 | 12 | 8 | 22 |

(a) A pie chart is to be drawn. Calculate the angle of the sector for each season.

(b) Explain why a pie chart is a suitable display for this data.

**Question 11**

The table shows the average maximum temperature in a town for the first six months of the year.

| Month | Jan | Feb | Mar | Apr | May | Jun |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Temperature ($^\circ$C) | 26 | 27 | 24 | 19 | 16 | 13 |

(a) Explain why a line graph is a good choice to display this data.

(b) Describe the trend in the temperature over the six months.

(c) Between which two months did the temperature fall the most? By how much did it fall?

**Question 12**

Eight students recorded their average daily screen time and their average hours of sleep per night.

| Screen time (hours) | 1 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sleep (hours) | 9.5 | 9 | 9.2 | 8.5 | 8 | 7.8 | 7 | 6.5 |

(a) Name the most suitable type of display for this data.

(b) Describe the relationship between screen time and sleep for these students.

(c) Mia says, "This proves that screen time causes students to sleep less." Is she correct? Explain.

**Question 13**

Two stores sold these numbers of bikes last year: Store A sold $80$ bikes and Store B sold $88$ bikes. A column graph of these sales has a vertical axis that starts at $76$ instead of $0$.

(a) On this graph, how many times as tall as Store A's column does Store B's column look?

(b) By what percentage did Store B's sales actually exceed Store A's sales?

(c) Explain why the graph is misleading, and how it should be fixed.

**Question 14**

For each situation, name a suitable display and give a reason for your choice.

(a) The percentage of a family's monthly budget spent on rent, food, transport and other costs

(b) Comparing the reaction times, in seconds, of $30$ Year 9 students with those of $30$ Year 12 students

(c) The number of visitors to a museum each year from 2015 to 2024

(d) The masses of $200$ newborn babies

**Question 15**

The time, $t$ minutes, that $50$ customers waited at a bank was recorded and shown on a histogram. The heights of the columns are given in the table.

| Waiting time (minutes) | $0 \le t < 5$ | $5 \le t < 10$ | $10 \le t < 15$ | $15 \le t < 20$ | $20 \le t < 25$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of customers | 8 | 14 | 15 | 9 | 4 |

(a) How many customers waited less than $10$ minutes?

(b) What percentage of customers waited at least $15$ minutes?

(c) Can you tell from the histogram exactly how long the longest waiting time was? Explain.

**Question 16**

Two schools surveyed all their Year 9 students about how they usually travel to school.

| Method | School X | School Y |
|---|---|---|
| Bus | 70 | 60 |
| Walk | 50 | 45 |
| Car | 80 | 45 |
| Total | 200 | 150 |

(a) For each school, write the number of students using each method as a percentage of that school's total.

(b) Sam says, "More School X students catch the bus, so catching the bus is more popular at School X." Is Sam right? Explain using your answers to (a).

(c) Name a display that would compare the two schools fairly, and explain why.

## Section C: Advanced (Questions 17-20)

**Question 17**

A consumer group tested the battery life, in hours, of $40$ phones of Brand P and $40$ phones of Brand Q. The five-number summaries for the two box plots are:

| | Minimum | Lower quartile | Median | Upper quartile | Maximum |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Brand P | 8 | 10 | 12 | 13 | 15 |
| Brand Q | 6 | 9 | 13 | 16 | 20 |

State whether each statement is true or false, and give a reason.

(a) Brand Q has the higher median battery life.

(b) Brand P has the larger interquartile range.

(c) At least half of the Brand Q phones lasted $13$ hours or more.

(d) About $75\%$ of the Brand P phones lasted $10$ hours or more.

(e) Which brand would you recommend to someone who wants a battery life that is reliable and predictable? Explain.

**Question 18**

The masses, in grams, of $20$ apples are:

$127, \ 104, \ 131, \ 119, \ 122, \ 142, \ 115, \ 128, \ 136, \ 120,$
$109, \ 125, \ 133, \ 112, \ 129, \ 138, \ 123, \ 145, \ 117, \ 130$

(a) Draw a frequency table using the classes $100 \le m < 110$, $110 \le m < 120$, $120 \le m < 130$, $130 \le m < 140$ and $140 \le m < 150$, where $m$ is the mass in grams.

(b) Which is the modal class?

(c) What percentage of the apples have a mass less than $120$ grams?

(d) Would a histogram or a column graph be more suitable for this data? Explain.

**Question 19**

The selling prices of the $9$ houses sold in a street last year were:

\$600,000, \$620,000, \$640,000, \$650,000, \$660,000, \$680,000, \$700,000, \$710,000 and \$2,120,000

(a) Find the mean selling price.

(b) Find the median selling price.

(c) Which measure better describes a typical selling price in this street? Explain.

(d) A real estate agent wants to make the street sound as expensive as possible. Which measure is the agent likely to quote?

**Question 20**

The stem-and-leaf plot shows the scores of $10$ players in a game. One leaf is missing and is shown as $\Box$. The leaves in each row are in order from smallest to largest. Key: $3 \mid 1$ means $31$.

| Stem | Leaf |
|---|---|
| 1 | 8 |
| 2 | 4 7 |
| 3 | 1 $\Box$ 5 9 |
| 4 | 0 6 |
| 5 | 2 |

The mean score is $34.5$.

(a) Find the missing score.

(b) Find the median score.

(c) The score of $52$ is changed to $62$. What happens to the mean and to the median? Give the new values.

# Data displays - Answer Key

**Question 1**

Answer: (a) Numerical, discrete (b) Categorical (c) Numerical, continuous (d) Categorical (it is ordered, so ordinal is also correct)

**Question 2**

Answer: (a) Line graph (b) Column graph (bar graph); a pie chart is also acceptable (c) Histogram (a stem-and-leaf plot, dot plot or box plot is also acceptable) (d) Scatter plot

**Question 3**

Answer: (a) Youngest $18$, oldest $53$ (b) $35$ years (c) $31$ years (the 8th value) (d) $25$ years

**Question 4**

Answer: (a) $80$ (b) $15\%$ ($\frac{12}{80} \times 100$) (c) $8$

**Question 5**

Answer: (a) $160 \le h < 165$ (b) $45\%$ ($\frac{18}{40} \times 100$) (c) $160 \le h < 165$: the median is the average of the 20th and 21st heights, and the first two classes hold only $10$ students while the first three hold $22$ (d) Height is continuous numerical data, so the classes join with no gaps.

**Question 6**

Answer: (a) $1$ goal (b) $2$ goals (c) $1.85$ goals ($\frac{37}{20}$) (d) $5$ goals

**Question 7**

Answer: (a) Class A $70$, Class B $77$ (b) Class A $39$, Class B $51$ (c) Class B, because its median ($77$) is higher (d) Class A, because its range ($39$) is smaller

**Question 8**

Answer: (a) $70$ (b) $25$ ($80 - 55$) (c) About $25\%$ (d) About $15$ days ($25\%$ of $60$)

**Question 9**

Answer: (a) Minimum $12$, $Q_1 = 17$, median $22$, $Q_3 = 29$, maximum $40$ (b) $12$ (c) The right (upper) whisker: it runs from $29$ to $40$ ($11$ minutes), while the left runs from $12$ to $17$ ($5$ minutes)

**Question 10**

Answer: (a) Summer $150^\circ$, Autumn $60^\circ$, Winter $40^\circ$, Spring $110^\circ$ (each person is $5^\circ$) (b) The data is categorical and the pie chart shows each season as a part of the whole group of $72$ people.

**Question 11**

Answer: (a) The data shows how one quantity changes over time, so joining the points shows the trend. (b) The temperature rises slightly from January to February, then falls steadily from February to June. (c) From March to April, a fall of $5^\circ$C

**Question 12**

Answer: (a) Scatter plot (b) A strong negative (linear) relationship: students with more screen time tend to get less sleep. (c) No. The data shows a relationship (correlation) only; it does not show that one causes the other, as other factors may be involved.

**Question 13**

Answer: (a) $3$ times as tall ($\frac{88 - 76}{80 - 76} = \frac{12}{4}$) (b) $10\%$ ($\frac{8}{80} \times 100$) (c) Starting the axis at $76$ makes a small difference look very large; the vertical axis should start at $0$.

**Question 14**

Answer: (a) Pie chart (or divided bar graph), because it shows parts of a whole (b) Parallel box plots (or a back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot), because they compare the centre and spread of two sets of numerical data (c) Line graph, because it shows change over time (d) Histogram, because there is a large amount of continuous numerical data that needs to be grouped

**Question 15**

Answer: (a) $22$ ($8 + 14$) (b) $26\%$ ($\frac{13}{50} \times 100$) (c) No. The histogram only shows that the longest waiting time was between $20$ and $25$ minutes, because the data is grouped.

**Question 16**

Answer: (a) School X: Bus $35\%$, Walk $25\%$, Car $40\%$. School Y: Bus $40\%$, Walk $30\%$, Car $30\%$ (b) No. School X has more bus travellers only because it has more students; as a percentage, catching the bus is more popular at School Y ($40\%$ compared with $35\%$). (c) A side-by-side (or stacked) column graph of the percentages, because percentages allow fair comparison of groups of different sizes.

**Question 17**

Answer: (a) True: $13 > 12$ (b) False: P's IQR is $3$ hours, Q's is $7$ hours (c) True: Q's median is $13$ (d) True: P's lower quartile is $10$ (e) Brand P, because its range ($7$) and IQR ($3$) are much smaller than Brand Q's ($14$ and $7$), so its battery life is more consistent.

**Question 18**

Answer: (a) Frequencies: $100 \le m < 110$: $2$; $110 \le m < 120$: $4$; $120 \le m < 130$: $7$; $130 \le m < 140$: $5$; $140 \le m < 150$: $2$ (b) $120 \le m < 130$ (c) $30\%$ ($\frac{6}{20} \times 100$) (d) A histogram, because mass is continuous numerical data grouped into classes.

**Question 19**

Answer: (a) \$820,000 ($\frac{7380000}{9}$) (b) \$660,000 (the 5th price) (c) The median, because the \$2,120,000 house is an outlier that pulls the mean above every other price. (d) The mean

**Question 20**

Answer: (a) $33$ (total $345$, known scores total $312$) (b) $34$ ($\frac{33 + 35}{2}$) (c) The mean rises by $1$ to $35.5$; the median stays at $34$.
